name: South Dakota
headline_status: Medical cannabis is legal for registered patients; recreational use remains illegal.
summary: South Dakota runs a voter-created medical cannabis program, in effect since July 1, 2021, and overseen by the state Department of Health. Voters approved recreational legalization in 2020, but the courts struck it down, and later legalization measures failed at the ballot in 2022 and 2024. Possessing marijuana without a patient card is still a crime, starting at a Class 1 misdemeanor for two ounces or less. No cannabis measure was on the November 2026 ballot.

medical_since.value: July 1, 2021, after voters approved Initiated Measure 26 in November 2020 (about 70% yes).

possession_limit.value: Registered patients may hold up to 3 ounces of cannabis, plus cannabis products in amounts set by Department of Health rules.

home_grow.value: Patients whose card allows cultivation may keep 2 flowering and 2 non-flowering plants, plus what those plants produce, at the grow site.

medical_program.value: A South Dakota-licensed physician, PA or APRN certifies a debilitating condition (e.g. cancer, chronic pain, epilepsy, MS, PTSD); the patient then applies online and pays a fee. About 19,800 patients were registered as of September 2026.

regulator.value: South Dakota Department of Health (Medical Cannabis Program).

retail_sales.value: Only state-certified medical dispensaries may sell, and only to cardholders; there is no adult-use retail.

penalties.value: Without a card, possessing 2 oz or less is a Class 1 misdemeanor; more than 2 oz is a felony, and courts may add civil penalties of up to $10,000.

timeline.event: Voters approve medical cannabis (IM 26) and recreational legalization (Amendment A).
A circuit judge strikes down Amendment A. The state Supreme Court later upholds that ruling.
The medical cannabis law takes effect.
Legislative rules committee approves the Department of Health's program rules.
Voters reject recreational measure IM 27 (47% yes).
Voters reject recreational measure IM 29 (44.5% yes).

faq.q: Is weed legal in South Dakota?
faq.a: Only for registered medical patients. Recreational cannabis is illegal: a 2020 voter-approved amendment was struck down in court, and legalization measures failed in 2022 and 2024.

faq.q: How much can a South Dakota medical patient possess?
faq.a: Up to 3 ounces of cannabis, plus products in amounts set by Department of Health rules. Patients with a cultivation endorsement may also grow 2 flowering and 2 non-flowering plants.

faq.q: What is the penalty for possession without a card?
faq.a: Two ounces or less is a Class 1 misdemeanor. Larger amounts are felonies, and courts can add a civil penalty of up to $10,000.

faq.q: How do I get a South Dakota medical card?
faq.a: A South Dakota-licensed physician, PA or nurse practitioner must certify a qualifying condition. You then apply through the Department of Health's online system and pay a fee.
